pre_data: Claims, the three counters and the shared counter library freeze before any claim artifact lands. Every constant is read with `git show <freeze>:reports/round-83/claims.json`, never from the graded tree. Each counter refuses (exit 2, `FAIL legs=0/<n> (refused: ...)`) a revision that is not 40-hex, a freeze that is not an ancestor of lands, lands equal to the frozen base (the do-nothing control), unreadable or incomplete frozen config, a leg list that disagrees with its own leg table, a lands revision that is not an ancestor of the branch tip, and a --work that is not an existing directory. Claim verdicts are graded on committed bytes only: each counter materialises the blobs it grades from --root:<rev> into <work>/tree before running any tool.

claims.kind: capability acquisition (a gate-registry coverage auditor) + the 11 standing registry rows
claims.title: Land tools/check-gate-registry.py and the missing gate-registry rows: every committed `reports/round-*/accept-*.py` counter has a row in SKILL.md `## Gates and probes`, derived and checked from committed bytes
claims.before: at base the registry stops at `accept-ca-75`: 58 committed accept-* counters, 11 of them with no row (`git ls-tree -r --name-only <base> reports | grep -E 'round-/(accept-.*\.py)$'` minus the entry-command cells of the `## Gates and probes` table). No committed instrument reads the registry: `git -C <lane> grep -c GATE-REGISTRY <base> -- tools/ reports/` = 0 lines.
claims.after: `tools/check-gate-registry.py` exists at lands and prints exactly one `GATE-REGISTRY: 0 missing / <r> registered / <i> instruments / 0 dead` line with i >= 61 and r >= (base rows + 14), exit 0; `--selftest` prints `SELFTEST: PASS (>=12 checks)`; the 11 base-missing counters and the 3 round-83 counters each appear in a row's entry-command cell, derived independently by the counter's own parse.
review_only: which additional tools/*.py deserve rows is a curation judgment; the tool reports the count (`GATE-REGISTRY-INFO`) and the round records it, it does not absorb it
the registry row prose quality (verdict maps, pinned values) is reviewed by a human-readable review seat, not counted

claims.after: the entry lands as the 257th knowledge file (>= 12000 bytes) with the header fields, >= 6 decision rows, >= 20 attested-anchor bullets each carrying exactly one distinct S-id, `tools/check-cited-lines.py` = 0 findings; SOURCES 832 -> >= 836 rows, the four new rows S909-S912 opened 2026-11-04, each `mined`, each `used-by` naming the entry; the entry cites at least three of those new rows.

claims.title: Land QUALITY criterion 31 (a cited record carries its bytes, a receipt cites resolvable repo-relative paths, a Gate names URL and access date per row) with tools/check-cited-records.py, and repair the round-82 record defects the non-author spot-check routed
claims.before: at base `corpus/QUALITY.md` has no `^31\. ` line, `reports/round-82/counter-revisions.md` is 0 bytes while three committed documents cite it as the r2/r3 record, no committed instrument reads cited-record integrity, S908's `teaches` cell opens `rejected:` (contract spelling `REJECTED:`) and its anchor cell names no chapter.
claims.after: `grep -c '^31\. ' corpus/QUALITY.md` = 1 with the three clauses; the record is > 400 bytes and names both revision hashes `696835ee` and `ea667212`; `reports/round-83/annotations/errata-r82.md` names `R82-M2`, `line 5` and `line 7`; a new registry row's `teaches` opens `supersedes S908 —` and carries `REJECTED:` plus a `chapter III` anchor; `tools/check-cited-records.py` prints `CITED-RECORDS: 0 empty / 0 scratch` exit 0 at lands and `SELFTEST: PASS (>=10 checks)`; existing registry rows differ only in their status/opened/recheck/used-by cells across base..lands.

do_nothing_control: At --lands = the frozen base every counter refuses with exit 2 (`FAIL legs=0/<n> (refused: lands equals the frozen base -- do-nothing control)`): a control that lands nothing cannot acquire the tool, open a source, add a criterion or fill the record. Receipts: reports/round-83/telemetry/controls-o.txt, controls-d.txt, controls-c.txt.
